## `pytest -p no:asyncio` masks all async test results

### Finding

During verification of PR #345 (wiki consolidation), running the full test suite with
`-p no:asyncio` caused all `@pytest.mark.asyncio` tests (`chapter_writer`, `setting_evolver`,
`character_evolver`, etc.) to fail. The correct invocation is plain `pytest` — the asyncio
plugin must remain active.

### Observation

`pytest-asyncio` 1.3.0 is installed in `.venv` and auto-registers as a plugin. Without it,
every `async def test_*` function is treated as a regular sync function that returns a coroutine
object — pytest sees the test as passing (the function "returned" without raising) but the async
body is never awaited. In other configurations it may raise a hard error. Either way the test
results are corrupted with no informative diagnostic.

This is a project-specific gotcha: `pyproject.toml` does not set `asyncio_mode = "auto"` and
does not declare `pytest-asyncio` as a dev dependency. Contributors who try to isolate the
asyncio plugin (e.g. to diagnose an unrelated warning) will destroy their test signal silently.

### Suggested Improvement

1. Add gotcha #054 to `.github/notes/gotchas.md` documenting the `-p no:asyncio` footgun.
2. Add a note to `.agents/skills/test-verification/SKILL.md` step 5 warning against this flag.

### Action Taken

Applied:
- Gotcha #054 added to `.github/notes/gotchas.md` (Testing section, after #053)
- `.agents/skills/test-verification/SKILL.md` step 5 updated with explicit asyncio warning
